_metadata.rubric: x02 rubric (owner style examples, clicks-when-explained bar, fewer phrase-joins, mechanism labelled, explanation checked), 2026-10-19
_metadata.independence: I read only the instructions file and the single input file x02-revision-review-input.json; no other files, repository search, web or paid API were used.

hints.reason: GOAT via billy goat (a male goat) and KID via the outlaw Billy the Kid, with the extra wink that a kid is also a young goat.

best_available.why: Two instantly familiar routes and a satisfying goat-family double layer.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent pair; the goat meaning of KID is a decoy that makes BILLY's outlaw route land nicely.

hints.reason: MORNING via morning dew on the grass and MOUNTAIN via Mountain Dew soda; both are instantly familiar, so this clears the exceptional phrase-join bar.

best_available.why: Clean, short, and both halves are household phrases.

pairs.pair_note: Mainly a ___ DEW join, but the morning side reads as a scene and the soda brand gives it pop-culture fun; passes as an exceptional phrase-join.

hints.reason: STRONG via Hercules' legendary strength and OLYMPUS via his ascent to the gods' home (also the Disney film's 'Go the Distance' goal).

best_available.why: One character who clearly owns both words.

pairs.pair_note: Solid shared-reference hint; explanation is accurate for the Roman/Disney framing.

hints.reason: HORSESHOE as a lucky charm and LEPRECHAUN as Lucky, the Lucky Charms mascot (plus Irish luck), so both sides click immediately.

best_available.why: Shared property with a cereal-box bonus; the horseshoe is even one of the marshmallow charms.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pair; the 'lucky charms' wordplay in the explanation is neat and brief.

hints.reason: HAWK via the name Tony Hawk and SKATEBOARD via Tony Hawk being the sport's most famous skater; the 1999 900 fact is correct.

best_available.why: One famous person ties both words together.

pairs.pair_note: Works through one person; slightly name-completion in feel but the skateboard side makes it a genuine reference rather than a mechanical fill-in.

hints.reason: INTERNET via Internet Explorer (and internet browsers generally) and SAFARI via Apple's Safari browser; clear once you read SAFARI as software rather than a trip.

best_available.why: Fair and direct; the reveal that SAFARI is the browser is mildly satisfying.

pairs.pair_note: Plain but fair; delight is modest. Internet Explorer is retired but still widely known.

hints.reason: IRELAND via its nickname the Emerald Isle and WIZARD via the Wizard of Oz's Emerald City; two famous green places.

best_available.why: Two well-known nicknames meeting in one jewel word; a real 'oh, nice' moment.

pairs.pair_note: Not a phrase-join with the target words themselves; it relies on knowledge of two famous emerald places, which is the kind of link the owner wants.

hints.reason: OAK via acorns being its seed and SQUIRREL via squirrels hoarding acorns; the forgotten-acorns-sprout fact is true and adds charm.

best_available.why: The perfect natural hint; the explanation ties both into one little life-cycle story.

pairs.pair_note: Easy but satisfying; good example of a one-idea explanation.

hints.reason: CINDERELLA via her midnight deadline and BALL via the royal ball she must flee as the clock strikes twelve; one iconic scene covers both.

best_available.why: Evokes the exact scene that holds both targets.

pairs.pair_note: Strong scene hint; BALL gets read as a sports ball first, which makes the reveal nicer.

hints.reason: MOVIE via popcorn at the theater and SNACK because popcorn is a classic snack; direct and fair.

best_available.why: The natural, obvious-in-a-good-way hint for this pair.

pairs.pair_note: On the nose but that is the pair's nature; 'generic' is not a reason to reject.

hints.reason: BILL via the one-dollar bill bearing Washington's face and BUCK as slang for that same dollar; factually correct.

best_available.why: One step removed from the dollar itself, avoiding a synonym while staying obvious after the reveal.

pairs.pair_note: Good indirect route; BILL and BUCK both have decoy meanings (bird beak, deer) that make the money reading a nice click.

hints.reason: ARCHAEOLOGY via Indiana Jones the archaeology professor and WHIP via his signature bullwhip.

best_available.why: Iconic character who owns both words; using the first name keeps it a satisfying leap.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent pop-culture shared reference.

hints.reason: CASINO via Las Vegas's famous casinos and ELVIS via Viva Las Vegas and his long Vegas residency; both facts are accurate.

best_available.why: A place that clicks with both targets at once.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; the explanation is accurate and brief.

hints.reason: PIG via the big bad wolf of The Three Little Pigs and CHIMNEY via the wolf climbing down the brick house's chimney in the classic telling.

best_available.why: One story scene contains both targets; CHIMNEY makes it a pleasant 'oh, that part' moment.

pairs.pair_note: Good scene hint; accurate to the familiar version of the tale.

hints.reason: FRIEND via Joey Tribbiani of the sitcom Friends and KANGAROO via joey meaning a baby kangaroo.

best_available.why: A textbook double meaning in the BARNEY/EVE style the owner likes.

pairs.pair_note: One of the best in the batch.

hints.reason: EARTH via the Earth's crust (its outer layer) and PIE via pie crust; a clean shared property, though the explanation's filling joke drifts off the point.
hints.fix: Rewrite the explanation as: "Earth's rocky outer layer is called its crust, just like the pastry shell of a pie."

best_available.why: Fair and satisfying layered-planet-as-pie image.

pairs.pair_note: Hint is good; the explanation's punchline about filling is a forced aside and should explain the connection instead.

hints.reason: SATELLITE via satellites travelling in orbit and GUM via the popular Orbit chewing-gum brand.

best_available.why: Word-plus-brand double meaning that clicks instantly once seen.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; the brand is widely sold in the U.S.

hints.reason: BONE via the humerus being the upper arm bone and HUMOR via its sound-alike pun with humorous (the classic 'funny bone' joke).

best_available.why: A well-known pun that delivers a genuine grin.

pairs.pair_note: Does not literally contain HUMOR (HUMER- vs HUMOR), so not contains_target; a sound-alike pun is fair here. Optionally the explanation could mention the funny bone.

hints.reason: PIG via Wilbur the pig of Charlotte's Web and LITTER via his being the runt Fern saves from the litter; accurate to the book.
LITTER via 'runt of the litter' is instant, but PIG is only moderate (runt piglets, or Wilbur via the explanation), since runts are just as often puppies or kittens.

best_available.why: A beloved character who links both sides, versus RUNT which leans on LITTER.

pairs.pair_note: WILBUR is the clear choice; RUNT is a weaker variant of the same idea, with the pig side borrowed from Wilbur.

hints.reason: ANGEL via angel food cake and DEVIL via devil's food cake; both are instantly familiar and the light/dark opposites make a genuinely satisfying pairing.

best_available.why: A rare phrase-join that is exceptional: both cakes are household names and the good/evil contrast is delightful.

pairs.pair_note: Passes as an exceptional phrase-join; players expecting a heaven/hell link get a pleasant surprise.

hints.reason: JAR via the cookie jar and INTERNET via browser cookies that track your browsing.

best_available.why: Edible versus digital cookie is a clean, widely known double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; everyone has clicked a cookie banner.

hints.reason: AXE via its chopping blade and HELICOPTER via its rotor blades; a fair shared property with a fun 'chopper' undertone.

best_available.why: Both objects plainly have blades; fair and quick to click.

pairs.pair_note: Pleasant rather than dazzling; nothing to repair.

hints.reason: TREE via Groot being a walking tree creature and GUARDIAN via his membership in the Guardians of the Galaxy.

best_available.why: A beloved, widely known character who is literally both targets.

pairs.pair_note: Strong pop-culture hint; MCU reach makes it broad rather than fandom-niche.

hints.reason: JOKE and ROAD both via the classic 'Why did the chicken cross the road?' joke.

best_available.why: The one famous joke that contains both targets.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent; the hint feels like a punchline in itself.

hints.reason: SCALE via Libra's scales and SCORPION via Scorpio; the two are indeed adjacent signs, so the explanation is accurate.

best_available.why: Recasts SCALE (fish, music, weight) as a star sign, a nice reveal.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; SCALE's many meanings make the zodiac reading satisfying.

hints.reason: BOND via his catchphrase 'shaken, not stirred' and COCKTAIL via the martini (and shaken cocktails in general).

best_available.why: One famous line delivers both; feels clever without being obscure.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent pop-culture quote hint; more satisfying than MARTINI would be.

hints.reason: WAITER via 'wait tables' and BUS via the restaurant verb 'bus tables'; it is a mechanical ___ TABLES fill-in, and the BUS side needs players to drop the vehicle reading first.
hints.fix: Rewrite the explanation as: "To bus tables is to clear them, and waiters wait tables."

best_available.why: The only hint offered; fair, but a fill-in phrase-join of the kind the owner wants fewer of.

pairs.pair_note: No PASS. The BUS-as-verb twist has some charm, but the link is a mechanical shared-object join, and 'Bussers bus tables' is a circular explanation.

hints.reason: GIFT via wrapping paper and MUMMY via its linen wrappings; a playful shared property.

best_available.why: A fun image (a mummy as a wrapped present) that clicks immediately.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; explanation is accurate and parallel.

hints.reason: POKEMON via Pikachu being its mascot and DETECTIVE via the 2019 film Detective Pikachu, where he wears a deerstalker cap.

best_available.why: The obvious Pokemon, made pair-specific by the Detective Pikachu film.

pairs.pair_note: Fair; the POKEMON side is easy and the DETECTIVE side depends on knowing the film, which is widely known.

hints.reason: HAMMER via Thor's hammer Mjolnir and MARVEL via Thor being a Marvel hero; the worthiness detail is accurate.

best_available.why: One character who clearly owns both targets.

pairs.pair_note: Solid if expected; nothing to repair.
